item: Ranks 9 and 10 of the 2026-09-30 diagnostics: per-route latency attribution, a timed browse and the unlock distance; K2 itself is unchanged
key_paths: src/monitoring/latency.py; src/monitoring/search_timing.py; src/monitoring/unlock_marker.py; src/monitoring/kpi.py; src/monitoring/benchmark.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; src/api/main.py; docs/product/RELEASE_0.4_GATE.md
summary: From the 16-instance diagnostics round of 2026-09-30: the K2 snappy bar read red on 16 of 16 instances, 287 of the 306 breaching routes (summed over the sixteen exports) on fewer than 20 samples, and GET /api/articles was its worst route on 8 of 16 with nothing timing a browse. Instruments only; no threshold, verdict or user-facing number changes. The latency summary lists every route (it cut at 60 and 20) and each row says how its window ended, its first call and the p95 without it, and its slowest call with its distance from the last unlock (absent, never 0, when no unlock finished); the K2 roll-up counts refusal- or error-driven, first-call-only and single-call breaches and its value, n and verdict are unchanged. The article list's browse is timed per phase (count_cached, count_recomputed or count_live, then rows) into a kinded, dated search-timing record that never enters the text aggregate; the benchmark times the first page through the real query; the self-test no longer empties the live window; the durable logs are cut by a copy swapped in with os.replace under one lock per log. The same PR closes row D of the 0.4 gate on instance 090243's release-run report and records PR #1281 in row A. Lesson: LESSONS.md, "A LIST THE PRODUCER CUT CANNOT BE LOOKED UP IN: A MISSING ROW READS AS NOBODY CALLED IT".
